title: Machine-readable parameter registry for the traffic-sweep analysis v2.4 (research/detection-time/sweep_analysis_v2.py; v2 at ac313f1, revised for protocol round 11, decisions 50-55 (v2.1, 6cd13a9), round 12, decision 57 (v2.2), round 13, decisions 58-59 with the v2.2 review (v2.3), and round 14, decision 60 with the v2.3 review (v2.4); system profiles and readers for TeaStore and OTel declared before any of their cells is read)
provenanceRule: Protocol decision 37 (research/PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md, round 8): every hyperparameter and sensitivity setting is traced to its origin. Human-readable source: research/protocol/PARAMETER_REGISTRY.md (84 rows, cb21c86). This file holds every value sweep_analysis_v2.py reads (status active) plus the four rows that registry left `unknown`, each with its resolution (status superseded / not-used-by-v2).

parameters.name: K_REFERENCE
parameters.origin_ref: decision 31 (round 8): K = 4 kept as the reference row; the value itself is dbebcbb's engineering default (detection_time.py:107)

parameters.name: K_GRID
parameters.origin_ref: Declared grid for the H7 fit (METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md H7; decision 42). Members: the Renard R10 preferred-number series (ISO 3) from 2.5 to 100, plus the literature values 3.0 (LIT_DETECTION_RULES.md D2, D4) and 3.5 (D3); 2.5 is D1's default, 4 the reference (decision 31), 3-5 the protocol grid (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md §3). The upper end (100, two decades above the literature) has no source: above it a family is reported as not certifiable by K.

parameters.name: MAD_SCALE
parameters.origin_ref: LIT_DETECTION_RULES.md D1 (Leys et al. 2013, doi 10.1016/j.jesp.2013.03.013: 'Usually, b = 1.4826, a constant linked to the assumption of normality') and D2 (Rousseeuw & Croux 1993, doi 10.1080/01621459.1993.10476408: 'we need to set b = 1.4826'). Resolves PARAMETER_REGISTRY.md unknown item 3.

parameters.name: FLOOR_REL_PRIMARY
parameters.origin_ref: decisions 27 (l) and 32 (round 8): floor = max(statistical threshold, 10 % of baseline median, resolution); LIT_DETECTION_RULES.md Q2 (Chromium 10 %, D13)

parameters.name: FLOOR_REL_ARM
parameters.origin_ref: decision 32: 5 % sensitivity arm; LIT_DETECTION_RULES.md Q2 (Hunter 5 %, D8)

parameters.name: RESOLUTION_RULE
parameters.value: min positive difference between two distinct values of one instrument inside one fault-free segment (one stream, one cell's fault-free time), minimum over the segments of the fit; for ledger latency (end - start of two float stamps) this is a float-difference granularity, not an instrument resolution, and never binding
parameters.origin_ref: Replaces SYS_FLOORS (PARAMETER_REGISTRY.md unknown item 2) and the absolute latency floors per decisions 27/32 ('clock resolution'). Instrument = (metric, collector, resource) for metrics, (span, jaeger) for span durations, (ledger) for ledger latency. Computed by sweep_analysis_v2.segment_stats(); fault-free data only; leave-one-cell-out for false alarms. Every value is printed in the readout. The ledger label is the v2 review's minor (readout-hotel-r3-v2-fix1/REVIEW.md, cb795c5).

parameters.name: MIN_BASELINE_POOLED
parameters.origin_ref: decision 31; METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md H1 ('Require n >= 20 baseline points, else —'). Applies to level thresholds and to the largest-gap scale of `absent`.

parameters.name: FAR_TARGET_PER_HOUR
parameters.origin_ref: decision 33 (round 8): '<= 15/h is the most the current quiet time certifies'; METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md H2 arithmetic: 4 no-fault cells x 180 s = 0.2 h per rate, 0 alarms -> exact 95 % bound 3/0.2 h = 15/h (LIT_DETECTION_RULES.md D21)

parameters.name: FAR_CONFIDENCE
parameters.origin_ref: LIT_DETECTION_RULES.md D21 (Hanley & Lippman-Hand 1983, doi 10.1001/jama.1983.03330370053031: 95 %, rule of three); used in H2's arithmetic

parameters.name: FAR_MEETS_CRITERION
parameters.value: upper
parameters.origin_ref: Reading of decision 33's 'certifies': a K meets the target when the exact one-sided Poisson upper bound (FAR_CONFIDENCE) of the held-out false-alarm rate is <= FAR_TARGET_PER_HOUR. The point-estimate reading ('point') is computed and reported beside it. Flagged for the user.

parameters.name: K_FIT_UNIT
parameters.value: family
parameters.origin_ref: decision 53 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 11): K is fitted per channel family within each system as the primary; the system-wide K is reported beside it. (v2 at ac313f1 had this as an engineering default departing from METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md H7's per-system K; the v2 review, M4, asked the user, who decided.) One K per (system, family): the smallest grid K that meets the target at every (class, rate) where some grid K meets it, counted on the class's scored set (CALIBRATION_SET_RULE); where none does the family is not at the operating point (—). The per-system K (one K for L, M, S, T together) is computed and reported beside.

parameters.name: MEDIAN_MIN_SAMPLES

parameters.name: ABSENT_GAP_MULT
parameters.origin_ref: detection_time.py:113 (dbebcbb); the gap is now pooled from fault-free data (H1, LIT_DETECTION_RULES.md table row 14)

parameters.name: ABSENT_REARM
parameters.origin_ref: Needed to define H2's restart-after-alarm false-alarm count (D17): `absent` fires at r + g for every record r followed by a silence longer than g, so it re-arms once the stream resumes. dbebcbb gave no verdict for the whole window when the stream was already silent at its start.

parameters.name: P3_TRAFFIC_INDEPENDENT

E.reason: the ledger observes requests: no request, no observation

L.reason: request-path log lines are emitted per request; the periodic templates (e.g. gRPC GoAway every 79-80 s) have no known mechanism linking them to these faults

M:cpu.reason: CPU usage is load-driven; the paused target's idle CPU is by construction (BC-idle-cpu) and its size depends on the load it had

S:sys_memory.reason: memory under hung requests grows with requests in flight (readout-hotel-r3/REVIEW.md, P3 row)

S:sys_psi_cpu.reason: of the throttled target it is actuator readback (decision 26, excluded); of any other service it is load-driven

parameters.origin_ref: decision 45 (round 9, H11): P3 restricted to signals traffic-independent by mechanism; actuator readback excluded by decision 26. Reasons are this registry's mechanism statements (engineering), one per family. With every flag false the set is empty and P3 is — for every fault.

parameters.name: LEDGER_ABSENT
parameters.origin_ref: METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md H3 (e), decision 42: the ledger gets `absent` on request completions (every request end, any outcome)

parameters.name: MARGIN_RULE
parameters.value: granularity(ledger stamp) + granularity(sensor stamp) + clock-alignment residual (per-cell fit wall = monotonic + offset over the ledger's startedAt/actualStartMonotonic and endedAt/actualEndMonotonic pairs, max |residual|) + for logs the per-cell receipt-delay bound
parameters.origin_ref: decision 35 (round 8, margin derived from measured timing uncertainty); METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md H3 (b). Granularity = 10^-d, d = the most fractional digits of the stamp's representation in the cell (ISO strings, Docker stamps, JSON floats); 1e-6 s for Jaeger microsecond integers; 1e-9 s for Kieker tin/tout and OTLP span timestamps (nanosecond integers; v2.2, TeaStore and OTel).

parameters.name: LOG_RECEIPT_RULE
parameters.value: per cell: max over log lines with both stamps of (Docker receive stamp - app stamp); Hotel app stamps are whole seconds, so the app stamp is the second boundary; a service whose lines carry no app stamp gets no bound and its log leads are not counted
parameters.origin_ref: METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md row 7 and H3 (b)

parameters.name: AVAILABILITY_SOURCES

value.E: the client's own end stamp (the ledger is written by the collecting client)
value.L: Docker daemon receive stamp (docker compose logs --timestamps)

parameters.unit: family -> measured collector receive stamp (null = none recorded)
parameters.origin_ref: decision 43 (round 9): event time primary; availability only from measured collector receive time. Span check: traces-normalized.json events and jaeger-raw(-remainder).json spans carry no receive stamp (key names are printed in the readout), so T availability is —.

parameters.name: P1_TOLERANCE_RULE
parameters.value: per episode: granularity(ledger stamp) + granularity(receipt stamp) + [pause: granularity(Docker event, 1e-9 s) + the cell's clock-alignment residual] + the cell's pre-onset median latency of successful requests
parameters.origin_ref: decision 54 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 11): 'The tolerance comes from measured timing terms', the terms as proposed in v2 (ac313f1). DECLARED BEFORE ANY TeaStore OR OTel CELL IS READ; on Hotel it was declared after the run (exploratory). Components: the timing-uncertainty margin of the sources involved (decision 35's principle) plus a bound on the time from send to the start of the response wait (the client's urllib socket timeout starts there, candidate_search.py _request); every successful request contains that time, so its fault-free median latency bounds it. Measured per cell from fault-free data.

parameters.name: P1_AMBIGUITY_WINDOW_RULE
parameters.value: pause: [fault-receipt startedMonotonic, Docker `pause` event of the target + delta]; delta = the cell's pre-onset median, over fault-free requests (ok, ended before startedMonotonic) whose trace has a span of the paused service, of (request end - the latest end of the paused service's spans in that request's trace), the span end mapped wall -> monotonic by the cell's fit; a request completing inside the window is ambiguous (it sets only the earliest expected timeout); no such request -> delta and P1 for the episode are —
parameters.origin_ref: decision 54 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 11), on the v2 review's M5 (readout-hotel-r3-v2-fix1/REVIEW.md, cb795c5): v2's interval assumed a request in flight at the freeze must time out; a request that passed the paused service before the pause event completes after it. DECLARED BEFORE ANY TeaStore OR OTel CELL IS READ.

parameters.name: LEDGER_ABSENT_TOKEN_RULE
parameters.value: the ledger's `absent` catch carries the token(s) of the first completion (any outcome) of the route after the silence; a sensor catch whose observation carries one of them is same-request (H3 c), no win; no completion after the silence -> no token
parameters.origin_ref: decision 51 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 11), on the v2 review's M1

parameters.name: SENSOR_ABSENT_TOKEN_RULE
parameters.value: a sensor's `absent` catch carries the token(s) of the observation that ends its silence (the stream's first record after the gap): its own token where it carries one (span: the token on the span itself, i.e. the tokened entry root; log: tokens named in the line), else the token(s) of the trace it belongs to (span: the trace's entry-root token, as the harness correlates it; log: the trace the line names, where the cell format carries one); if that request is the ledger's catching request the pair is same-request (H3 c, no win); with neither (no observation ends the silence, or the ending one carries no token and belongs to no tokened trace) the pair is unclassifiable: no win, counted and reported per rate
parameters.origin_ref: decision 57 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 12, d126589): the mirror of decision 51; the trace fallback and the unclassifiable class are the coordinator's brief for v2.2 (2026-10-04). DECLARED BEFORE ANY TeaStore OR OTel CELL IS READ.

parameters.name: SCALE_NOT_ESTIMABLE_RULE
parameters.value: a sensor (incl. a ledger route's latency) with >= MIN_BASELINE_POOLED pooled fault-free points and MAD = 0 in the fit used is 'scale not estimable': its level rules (spike, run3, median) give —, no catch and no false alarm, and it is listed; appear and absent are kept; no quantile threshold
parameters.origin_ref: decision 52 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 11), on the v2 review's M2; the quantile-based threshold (empirical upper quantile + resolution) is a later sensitivity row, writing todo W2

parameters.name: CALIBRATION_SET_RULE
parameters.value: held-out false alarms are counted per fault class on that class's scored sensor set: the spike path filter (dt.scored with the class's target and affected path) and the by-construction flags (bc_of with the class's target and fault kind, no-BC view as P4) applied per rule and direction exactly as in scoring; a fire that is not admitted mutes its sensor-rule until the next restart; the detector restarts after each counted alarm; the ledger keeps its BC catches (as in scoring); v2's all-sensors count is reported beside it, labelled
parameters.origin_ref: decision 55 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 11, engineering consistency named by the coordinator), on the v2 review's M3: 'the detector calibrated must equal the detector scored'

parameters.name: P4_NOT_EVALUABLE_RULE
parameters.value: P4 at a (class, rate) is — (not evaluable) when the ledger E or a collected sensor family (L, M, S, T) is not at the operating point there; highest_rate names every — rate as '— at {rates}'
parameters.origin_ref: decision 55 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 11, B1 of the v2 review)

parameters.name: V1_REFERENCE_POINT
parameters.origin_ref: v1's declared reference point (sweep_analysis.py REF = dbebcbb's setting K = 4, floor 1 ms; DECLARATION.md a795fc9 analysis row). v2.1 uses it only to re-run v1 in process for the v1 moved-verdicts table when v1's readout is not given.

parameters.name: EXPOSURE_RULE
parameters.value: route call path = services reachable from the entry over parent->child service edges of tokened, entry-rooted traces in the no-fault cells, plus `data store` services (project-map role rule) that a path service depends_on in the no-fault cells' compose-rendered.yml; exposed iff >= 1 ledger request started in [onset, hold end] and the sensor's service is on that path
parameters.origin_ref: METHODOLOGY_HARDENING.md H5, decision 42 (exposure recorded, objective unchanged). The data-store extension is an engineering default: Hotel's data stores emit no spans of their own, so trace adjacency alone cannot project them.

parameters.name: REPORT_TOP_SOURCES
parameters.unit: sensors listed per (family, rate) in the readout text
parameters.origin_ref: display only: the readout lists the sensor/rule sources of the alarms left at the largest grid K, the most frequent first; the JSON keeps all of them. No verdict depends on it.

parameters.name: CLOCK_RULE_TEASTORE
parameters.value: the analysis monotonic clock is the journey ledger's (seconds from fixed_load's barrier); wall = mono + offset fitted on the ledger's startedAt/endedAt pairs (MARGIN_RULE's fit); the producer's offsets (intervention, probes; relative to receipt.window.measurementStartMonotonic) map to wall as measurementStartedAt + offset and then to the ledger clock by the fit; the largest deviation of the intervention's own wall/offset pairs from that mapping is the receipt-alignment residual, added to P1's tolerance; system samples are timed at their `monotonic` stamp (after the read) mapped the same way
parameters.origin_ref: harness 91c4967: modules/teastore/execution/performance_campaign.py:2395 (producer barrier = time.monotonic()+15, offsets relative to it), modules/teastore/workload/fixed_load.py:928 (the ledger's barrier derived from the same epoch in another process), modules/teastore/collectors/system_probe.py:82 (`monotonic` after the read; `epoch`/`at` are the scheduled target). DECLARED BEFORE ANY TeaStore OR OTel CELL IS READ.

parameters.name: SILENCE_START_TOKEN_RULE
parameters.value: an `absent`-vs-`absent` pair (a sensor's `absent` against the ledger's `absent`) is same-request (H3 c, no win) if the silence-STARTING records share a request token OR the silence-ENDING records do (decision 57's test, unchanged). The starting record is the last observation before the silence on each channel: the ledger's last completion before its silence (its tokens), the sensor's last observation before its silence (its own token, else its trace's entry-root token, as decision 57). A pair with a token missing on either start, not already same-request, is unclassifiable (no win, counted). Mixed pairs (only one side `absent`) keep decision 57 / 51. Every absent-vs-absent lead is reported with its decomposition: (ledger's last completion - sensor's last observation, each from the onset in its own clock) + (g_ledger - g_sensor) + residual (clipping at the onset, a whole-second log stamp, a catch moved out of a probe window).
parameters.origin_ref: decision 58 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 13, 6162c37), on the independent v2.2 review (Fable adversarial-review, 2026-10-05, of 421a6d2 / freeze 5c98726) F1: for an absent/absent pair the silence-starting records set the lead. DECLARED BEFORE ANY TeaStore OR OTel CELL IS READ.

parameters.name: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS

value.F7: TeaStore fixture cells are written by the harness's test writer (tests/test_teastore_traffic_sweep.py make_sweep_run), which writes resources.json in every cell; the producer writes it in no-fault cells only (modules/teastore/execution/performance_campaign.py:1690-1693). The reader never reads M on TeaStore (FAMILY_CHANNELS), so the fixture difference is untested, not a reader path.
value.F9: TeaStore S samples are placed on the wall clock through the producer's barrier pair (CLOCK_RULE_TEASTORE), not the ledger fit; the P4 margin of an S-vs-ledger lead omits that mapping term, which P1's tolerance includes (receipt-alignment residual). Immaterial at a 5 s cadence; recorded.
value.F10: OTel cell validity is the target-side receipt.json state (it folds in F1/G1/G2/G4, trace completeness and container health); the coordinator-side terminal replay (candidate_terminal.validate_campaign, remote-terminal.json) is not read. TeaStore reads the validator's candidate-validation.json.
value.F11: The harness refuses a cell when one token maps to several Kieker traces, and (woven entry point) when one trace maps to several tokens (modules/teastore/witness/extract_native_token_correlation.py:449-467); the reader drops such bridge rows instead and counts them (readout: reader statistics, bridgeTokensWithSeveralTraces / bridgeTracesWithSeveralTokens). On harness-validated cells both counts are expected 0.
value.G4: OTel: productcatalogservice logs through logrus's default TextFormatter (upstream src/productcatalogservice/main.go:57, not JSON) and frontend writes plain console output, so neither carries an app stamp the reader parses (JSON_LOG_STAMP_RULE notParsed): their L leads read "log lead not counted (no app stamp)" and their lines do not enter LOG_RECEIPT_RULE's bound. Recorded, not fixed (a logfmt reader would be a new layout).

parameters.name: START_TERM_RULE
parameters.value: an `absent`-vs-`absent` pair that decisions 57 and 58 leave neither same-request nor unclassifiable (different requests start and end the two silences) is a win only if its START term (the ledger's last completion before its silence - the sensor's last observation before its silence, each from the onset in its own clock, i.e. on the common clock through the cell's alignment) exceeds the tie margin (MARGIN_RULE; on the availability clock its availability margin); the gap term (g_ledger - g_sensor) never counts toward a lead and stays printed in the decomposition; a pair whose start term cannot be computed is no win; category 'start term within the margin (decision 60)'. Mixed pairs (only one side `absent`) are unchanged.
parameters.origin_ref: decision 60 (PROTOCOL_DRAFT_20261002.md round 14, c17f6a6), on the v2.3 follow-up review's G2: the gap term is a difference between two fitted thresholds whose estimation uncertainty is not in the tie margin. DECLARED BEFORE ANY TeaStore OR OTel CELL IS READ.
